evidence:
io.lisp:4366-4367
  (defun fnn-archive-read-dir (dir sub)
    (sort (copy-list (fnn-list-directory (fnn-join dir sub))) #'string<))
io.lisp:4685-4686
  (config-names (fnn-archive-read-dir dir "config"))
  (record-names (fnn-archive-read-dir dir "records"))
The docstring at 4538-4541 says: "No list of the archive's records, and never the MANIFEST as one list, is built: the work and allocation per step are one chunk's." Elsewhere the log uses fnn-list-directory-bounded (7233); here the listing is unbounded and sorted. The import runs both passes (4571, 4620), so it is listed twice.
fix: Stream records/ in the MANIFEST's order: ask ACL2 for the next expected entry name, or read the directory in bounded batches and refuse past a profile-derived count. Alternatively, make the docstring state the O(entries) name list honestly and bound it through fnn-list-directory-bounded with a named refusal.
reviewer: Confirmed. fnn-archive-read-dir (io.lisp:4366-4367) builds the full fnn-list-directory list (659-670, unbounded) and sorts a copy of it. fnn-import-pass binds record-names at 4686 before any chunk is read, and the import runs that pass twice (4571 and inside fnn-log-write-history at 4620). Export writes one file per record (4323, with the per-record loop at 4335ff), so even a genuine archive of an N-record history yields N names. Memory therefore grows with the archive, not with one chunk. That contradicts the docstring's claim (4538-4541) and the D27 work-bound rule; the log path already uses fnn-list-directory-bounded for its own listing. Practical impact is a large-history or adversarial-archive import on a small-memory node (the 2 GB friend node) running out of heap instead of giving a named refusal. It is an offline operator verb.
scenario: An archive is external input (the comment at 4369-4373 says so). An archive with millions of entries in records/, real or adversarial (empty or junk files the MANIFEST check rejects only after the listing), makes `store import` allocate and sort every name up front, twice, before the first MANIFEST mismatch can stop it. Memory grows with the archive, not with one chunk. On the 2 GB OpenBSD friend node that ends in heap exhaustion instead of a named refusal.
title: Import builds the whole records/ directory listing in memory, contradicting its one-chunk allocation claim
